question.problem: A triangle has sides $m$, $n$, and $o.$ The sides $m$, $n$, and $o$ are of lengths  $2$, $5$, and $6$, respectively. What is the measure of the angle between the sides $n$ and $o?$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252321/assets/26f2041aec84bb0086e2f08c2ba3a19331895951782b7fda153858643a8a5dd4.png)

We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $M:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡M & =\frac{{o}^{2}+{n}^{2}-{m}^{2}}{2no}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Here, we have

$$
m=2,\,n=5,\,o=6.
$$

This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡M & =\frac{{6}^{2}+{5}^{2}-{2}^{2}}{2(5)(6)} \\  & =\frac{36+25-4}{60} \\  & =\frac{57}{60}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠M & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{57}{60}) \\  & ={18.19}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
